approach: Add to crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs a pure, stack-aware `plan_rebase` and a free function `rebase_job_branch`, and re-export them from gh/mod.rs. `plan_rebase` takes git, the new base (`onto`), the local branch head, the job's own landing commit, the verified fingerprint, the rules commit and `sign`. It returns Current, Moved, or Conflict. It replays the first-parent commits between the fork and the head one at a time onto `onto`, using the same three-way step as `Git::replay`: `merge_tree(parent, tip, commit)`, then `commit_tree` with the old message. The only new git call is `git merge-base`, through `Git::run`, because athena-git has no helper for it. A commit that conflicts and is not the job's own is carried as a records-only commit. That commit is built with the existing `Git::commit_with_records(parent, commit, ..)`, which gives the parent's tree with the commit's `records/` paths. It is then merged onto the running tip with `merge_tree(parent, tip, records_image)`. So its `records/` paths are kept and its code paths are dropped. The carried message has its trailers removed and a note added, so the commit cannot be mistaken for the job's landing commit. A conflict in the job's own commit gives `Conflict`, and no ref moves. `rebase_job_branch(git, state, remote_name, default_branch, job, verified_fp, rules_commit, sign, ui)` does the following. It refuses to rebase (`Unchecked`) when the work branch on the remote holds anything other than the stored early head. It fetches origin's default branch. It finds the landing commit with `landed_commit_for`. It takes the repository lock. It runs `plan_rebase`. On `Moved` it runs `reset_keep(tip)` and prints one status line. It never pushes. Tests use real temporary repositories and a real bare origin, with no mocks. The drain is not touched. CHANGELOG.md and async-drain.md get notes. The CHANGELOG entry and the design-doc note state: clean earlier unlanded commits still ride along in the next pull request, the re-check rule does not cover stacked content, a conflicting earlier commit is kept as records only, queue order is pass order, and the drain wiring is a follow-up.

decisions.choice: A conflicting earlier commit is carried as a records-only commit. The helper is `Git::commit_with_records(parent, commit, ..)`, then `merge_tree(parent, tip, that_image)`. The carried message drops the Athena-* trailers and gets a note that the code was held back.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 2 and the user's ruling. Its `records/` paths stay on the branch, so `Records::load` from the new tip still sees the held-back job. `commit_with_records(parent, commit)` builds the parent's tree with the commit's records, so the later three-way merge from the parent applies only the commit's own record changes and never replaces records that earlier carried commits added. It uses an existing public athena-git API, so athena-git stays untouched. Trailers are dropped so that `landed_commit` (pre-C0, which finds a commit by its Athena-Job and Athena-Verified-Content trailers) cannot select the code-less commit as that job's landing commit.

rejected.option: Skip a conflicting earlier commit and leave it off the branch (the round-3 left-behind rule)
rejected.why: It drops the job's records from the branch, which is the deferred drop_landed by another name. This is finding 2.

rejected.option: Replace all of `records/` with the commit's `records/` snapshot at the tip
rejected.why: It would erase records that earlier carried commits added.

rejected.option: Hold back every job stacked above a conflicting commit
rejected.why: The next candidate would never land in the stacked shape.

decisions.choice: A conflict in the job's own landing commit returns `Rebase::Conflict { commit, text }`. No ref moves, nothing is pushed, there is no retry, and there is no stop. A conflict in the records-only merge of an earlier commit is also `Conflict`, naming that commit. A first-parent commit with no parent in the range is an `Err`, not a `Conflict`.
decisions.reason: This is the hold-back the user asked for. A records conflict is a conflict between job records, which an operator must see. A parentless commit is a repository fault, not a conflict, and must not read as a hold.

rejected.why: It would hide real errors as a hold-back.

decisions.choice: `plan_rebase` checks `Current` first: when `onto` is an ancestor of the job's landing commit, it returns `Current` and replays nothing. Otherwise it replays `fork..head`, where fork comes from `git merge-base onto head`. The commits after the job's own commit (later jobs stacked above) are carried with the same rule, and the new tip is the whole rebuilt branch.
decisions.reason: `reset_keep(tip)` moves the whole local branch, so commits stacked above the job must be carried or they would be lost. `Current` also covers the group-job path today. After `resync_onto_merge`, main is already an ancestor of the next job's commit.

rejected.why: Jobs and records stacked above the head would vanish when the branch moves.

decisions.choice: `Moved` carries `content_changed: bool`. It is true when the governed fingerprint of the replayed landing commit's tree differs from the verified fingerprint. It is computed with `athena_git::attrs::fingerprint` under `rules_commit`. `plan_rebase` never refuses on it.
decisions.reason: The request names no re-check outcome. The re-check rule is build job 7. The drain follow-up needs to know that verified content moved. Landing is not blocked here, and `land_pr`'s merged-content check stays the safety net. A report-only flag keeps this half small and loses no information.

rejected.option: Return NeedsRecheck and refuse to move
rejected.why: Any change to governed content on main would block every rebase, so the acceptance case (main moved, second job lands rebased) would not hold. It also pre-empts job 7.
The follow-up would have to recompute it, and the CHANGELOG would hide a real gap.

decisions.choice: The CHANGELOG entry and async-drain.md state that earlier unlanded commits which replay cleanly still ride along in the next job's pull request, as today. They also state that the re-check rule does not cover stacked content, that queue order is pass order and not stacking order, and that the drain wiring is a follow-up job. The queue-order note extends the first-half note at async-drain.md lines 137-141.
decisions.reason: This answers findings 3 and 4 by stating the facts instead of claiming a guarantee the code does not give.

rejected.option: Treat known not-landed jobs' code like a conflicting commit
rejected.why: It needs record state the drain wiring owns, and it is outside this slice.

rejected.option: Order the queue by position on the local branch
rejected.why: It changes drain.rs, which is out of scope.

decisions.choice: `rebase_job_branch` takes `git`, `state: &StateDir`, `remote_name: &str` and `default_branch: &str`, and builds `GitRemote { git, name }` itself. The flow is: (1) published-head rule: the work branch on the remote is absent or equals `load_early(state, job)`, otherwise `Unchecked(reason)`. (2) `git.fetch_remote_branch(remote_name, default_branch)`; a failure or none found is `Unchecked`. (3) `landed_commit_for` on the head; none found is `Unchecked`. (4) `state.lock_repository()`, re-read the head, `plan_rebase`. (5) On `Moved`, `reset_keep(tip)` and one `ui.line`; a refused reset is an `Err`. `Rebase` has the variants Current, Moved{onto, landed, tip, records_only: Vec<String>, content_changed}, Conflict{commit, text} and Unchecked(String).
decisions.reason: It runs against a real bare origin in tests and never pushes. A network failure or an already-published head must not become 'not landed', and `land_pr` keeps replacing the head only when it is the early head, so the published-head rule keeps today's cases working.

rejected.why: The fetch needs the remote's name anyway, and a real bare origin is a stronger test than a fake.
`resync_onto_merge` takes it for the same branch rewrite.
It adds a push path to `land_pr`, which is out of scope.

decisions.choice: gh/mod.rs gets a one-line widening of the existing `pub use landing::{..}` list (lines 51-54) with `Rebase`, `plan_rebase` and `rebase_job_branch`.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 1. The brief now lists gh/mod.rs as a deliverable. The `landing` module is private, so athena-cli cannot name the items otherwise.

rejected.why: The drain follow-up could not call them.

steps: Read in landing.rs the imports (lines 4-21), `landed_commit_for` and `Athena::land_pr`. Read the land.rs tests (~351-526) and `fixtures` (line 243), gh/tests.rs `records_flow::World` (~1971) and test_support.rs `land_through_pr` (line 606). Read `Git::replay`, `merge_tree`, `commit_tree`, `commit_with_records`, `reset_keep` and `fetch_remote_branch` in athena-git, and `store::Records::load` (store.rs:309).

In landing.rs add `Rebase` (Current, Moved{onto, landed, tip, records_only, content_changed}, Conflict{commit, text}, Unchecked(String)). Add `pub fn plan_rebase(git, onto, head, landed, verified_fingerprint, rules_commit, sign) -> Result<Rebase>`: Current if `onto` is an ancestor of `landed`. Otherwise fork = `git.run(["merge-base", onto, head])`, then the first-parent commits in `fork..head` oldest first. For each: its first parent (none is an Err); `merge_tree(parent, tip, commit)`; a clean merge is committed with the old message unless the tree equals the tip's. A conflict at `landed` returns Conflict. A conflict elsewhere builds `commit_with_records(parent, commit, note, sign)` and merges it onto the tip; the note is the old subject, the old body without trailers, and a line saying the code was held back by a rebase conflict. A conflict there is Conflict naming the commit. Record the commit in `records_only`. Remember the replayed commit for `landed`. `content_changed` compares `athena_git::attrs::fingerprint` of its tree with the verified one.

Add the `#[cfg(test)] mod rebase_tests` plan_rebase cases: plan_rebase_clean_move, plan_rebase_already_current, plan_rebase_conflict_in_own_commit, plan_rebase_earlier_conflict_is_records_only (including the Records::load and path assertions), plan_rebase_clean_earlier_commit_is_carried, and one with a parentless commit giving Err. Run `cargo test -p athena-core plan_rebase` before going on.

Add `pub fn rebase_job_branch(git, state, remote_name, default_branch, job, verified_fingerprint, rules_commit, sign, ui) -> Result<Rebase>` with the flow of decision 5, and add the bare-origin tests: rebase_job_branch_lands_second_job_on_the_moved_main, rebase_job_branch_conflict_changes_nothing, and the two Unchecked extras. Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Confirm `git diff --stat` lists only the four deliverables.

risks.risk: A records-only commit is classed as a JobLanding for the held-back job in the next job's pull request (see the first open question).
risks.mitigation: The carried message has its Athena-* trailers removed and a note added, so the trailer lookup (`landed_commit`, pre-C0) cannot pick it. The post-C0 records lookup caveat is named in async-drain.md and the CHANGELOG, and left to the drain follow-up that returns the job. A clean earlier commit already rides along today in the same way.

risks.risk: A held-back job's records may be changed by the records-only merge if they overlap other carried records.
risks.mitigation: `merge_tree(parent, tip, records_image)` is a three-way merge restricted to that commit's own records changes. A conflict there returns `Conflict` naming the commit and moves nothing. A core test pins the carry.

risks.risk: Rebasing makes the governed fingerprint of the landed commit differ from the verified one, so a later merged-content check reports merged-unverified.
risks.mitigation: `content_changed` reports it and the status line shows it. This half adds no re-check. The merged-content check in `land_pr` stays the safety net. Job 7 decides the re-check.

risks.risk: After a rebase the local branch moved while the pull request's remote head already holds an earlier landing commit.
risks.mitigation: The published-head rule makes the result `Unchecked` and nothing moves. A test covers it. The cut line allows reporting that test as a read-only check.

risks.risk: The producer run is long: about 10 tests, with bare-origin setup.
risks.mitigation: The cut line: the Moved test and every plan_rebase test must run. The conflict case against the bare origin and the two Unchecked extras may be reported as read-only checks. Nothing in drain.rs or the athena-cli tests is touched.

risks.risk: Clippy or fmt failures from new code.
risks.mitigation: Every new item is `pub` and exported. No `#[allow]` is added. Step 6 runs the three checks.

risks.risk: Replaying with `commit_tree` signs commits only when `sign` is set.
risks.mitigation: The caller passes `git.signs_commits()?`, as `resync_onto_merge` does (land.rs line 195). Tests pass false.

demonstrations.method: Tests in a `#[cfg(test)] mod rebase_tests` inside landing.rs call the production `plan_rebase` on real temporary git repositories made with `Git::isolated` and `git init`, with real commits built by `crate::land::fixtures::commit/landed/plain`. Both exist today: `pub(crate) mod fixtures` in land.rs line 243, and the repo helper in the land.rs tests (~line 351, copied locally). Cases: (a) `plan_rebase_clean_move`: main gets an outside commit, the job's landing commit sits on the old main. (b) `plan_rebase_already_current`: onto is an ancestor of the landing commit. (c) `plan_rebase_conflict_in_own_commit`: main and the job's commit edit the same line. (d) `plan_rebase_earlier_conflict_is_records_only`: stack of b then c, b conflicts with the new main, c is disjoint. (e) `plan_rebase_clean_earlier_commit_is_carried`: stack of b then c, both replay cleanly. There is no mock. The seam is the real repository.
demonstrations.observes: (a) Moved: the new landing commit's parent is the outside commit's main tip, its message and trailers equal the old ones, and `content_changed` is true. (b) Current, and no ref moved. (c) Conflict naming the job's own commit, and the main ref and branch tip unchanged. (d) Moved with `records_only` equal to [b's commit], and the tip's parent chain is onto, then b's records-only commit, then c. (e) Moved with `records_only` empty, and the tip holds b's file and c's file.
demonstrations.fails_without: If plan_rebase did not replay, the clean-move test would see no new parent chain. Without the first-parent conflict check, the conflict test would get Moved or an Err, not Conflict. Without the records-only carry, the earlier-conflict test would see either a Conflict or a branch missing the earlier job's records/ paths. Without the Current check, the already-current test would see Moved.
demonstrations.seam: Production `plan_rebase` called directly. Real repositories from `Git::isolated` plus `land::fixtures`. These exist today (read in land.rs). Step 3 adds the plan_rebase tests.

demonstrations.method: The test `plan_rebase_earlier_conflict_is_records_only` from criterion 1 goes further. b's landing commit is built with `fixtures::landed(job_b)` for its records and `fixtures::plain` for a code file that conflicts with the moved main. c's commit uses `fixtures::landed(job_c)` and a disjoint code file. After `plan_rebase` for c, the test reads the new tip. It calls `git.show_file(tip, <b's code path>)`, `git.ls_tree`/`show_file` for b's `records/` paths, and `crate::store::Records::load(&git, &tip)`. `Records::load` is the production loader that `land_pr` uses (landing.rs line 431). The whole athena-core suite runs, so the new tests also run with every existing one.
demonstrations.observes: At the new tip, b's code path is absent and b's `records/` paths are present. `Records::load(&git, &tip)` returns jobs for both b and c, and b's candidate, verification and outcome records are readable. The suite passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the records-only carry dropped records/, or kept the code paths, the path assertions fail. If it replaced all of records/ with a snapshot, c's record would be missing and Records::load would lack job c. Without the carry, `Records::load` at the new tip would not contain b's job.
demonstrations.seam: Production `plan_rebase` and `Records::load` on a real repository. The fixtures exist (land.rs line 243). The test is added in step 3. Whether `Records::load` accepts the fixtures' repository is unproven and is settled by running the test.

demonstrations.method: Tests in landing.rs call the production `rebase_job_branch` against a real bare origin. The origin is `git init --bare` in a temp directory. The work repository, made with `Git::isolated`, has `origin` pointing at it. The work repository has two jobs' landing commits stacked on one local branch. A third repository, or the work repository, then pushes an outside commit to the bare main after the second job was verified. `StateDir::new(tempdir)` is the state. The Quiet or recording Ui from the crate's tests is used. The producer reads `records_flow::World` (gh/tests.rs ~1971) and `test_support` for the setup shape and copies the minimum; the seam is the real bare repository. Cases: `rebase_job_branch_lands_second_job_on_the_moved_main` and `rebase_job_branch_conflict_changes_nothing`. A cheaper extra pair, `rebase_job_branch_unchecked_when_origin_is_unreachable` and `rebase_job_branch_unchecked_for_a_published_head`, is part of the plan.
demonstrations.observes: First case: the result is Moved. `git log --first-parent --format=%H` on the local branch is linear. The second job's new landing commit has the bare main's tip as an ancestor. The first job's commit rides along. Second case: Conflict, the local branch tip equals the old tip, and the bare main equals the old main. Extras: Unchecked, with no ref moved.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the replay in rebase_job_branch, job 2's landing commit would stay on the old main and the parent-is-origin-main assertion would fail. Without the conflict path, the local branch or the bare main would move or the call would return Err.
demonstrations.seam: Production `rebase_job_branch`, with git, the state dir and the remote name passed as arguments. A real bare origin. The test is added in step 4; the Ui and StateDir helpers exist. Cut line: if the run is long, the conflict case and the two Unchecked extras may be reported as read-only checks. The Moved case and the plan_rebase tests are never cut.

open_questions: A records-only commit for a held-back job b still adds b's closing records. The gate's `classify_pre_merge` (athena-gate invariant.rs:320) classes a commit that adds closing records as a JobLanding without comparing the governed fingerprint, so b's records could appear as a landing in c's pull request. After C0, `landed_commit_from_records` finds a landing by its records and could pick the records-only commit as b's landing commit. This slice does not wire b to land again. Should the drain follow-up (A6b, send_back) handle this? I assume yes and name it in async-drain.md.
`Moved.content_changed` is report-only here. The re-check rule is build job 7. Is a flag with no refusal acceptable for this half? I assume so. It is stated in the CHANGELOG and the doc note.

Whether `Records::load` (store.rs:309) loads the repository the `land::fixtures` build is not proven. The producer settles it by running the records-only test. The fallback is to assert the record paths through `show_file`, and then to say so in the report.

The bare-origin setup is copied from `records_flow::World` (gh/tests.rs ~1971) and `test_support`. I did not read those lines. The producer reads them first, and falls back to `git init --bare` plus `git remote add origin <path>` with `Git::isolated`.
